articles.headline: Wall Street rallies sharply as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive
articles.title: Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.summary: Main United States stock indexes surged on Monday, November 23, 2026, driven by a record 32.2% jump in Nvidia shares after the chipmaker reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. The Nasdaq Composite climbed 6.69% to 24,131.42, fueled by widespread gains across artificial intelligence and tech stocks. Investors now await upcoming inflation data from Wednesday's personal consumption expenditures report to gauge Federal Reserve monetary policy.
articles.description: Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Jensen Huang’s return

articles.headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive following government consultations
articles.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after U.S. government input
articles.summary: Nvidia unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive on Monday, November 23, 2026, after board members received assurances from senior United States government officials that he posed no national security risk. The decision followed public backing from President Donald Trump, occurring less than two weeks after the 63-year-old co-founder resigned over an alleged spy scandal involving former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang.
articles.description: U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision”

articles.headline: Iran vows to use all means to counter United States naval blockade

Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei stated during a press briefing that Tehran views the blockade as military aggression, invoking Article 51 of the United Nations Charter for self-defense amid ongoing regional conflict.
articles.description: War broke out between Iran and the United States on February 28 when U.S.-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei

articles.headline: COP31 climate talks collapse in Antalya over fossil fuel phase-out standoff
articles.title: COP31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out
articles.summary: United Nations climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkiye, concluded without consensus on November 22, 2026, after a record 48-hour overtime due to disagreements over fossil fuel language. The European Union, backed by roughly 130 nations, rejected the cover text for lacking phase-out commitments. Conversely, nations like India and Saudi Arabia supported the text, stressing the need for equitable energy transitions.
articles.description: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

articles.headline: UN COP31 climate talks in Turkey end without major deal
articles.title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed
articles.summary: United Nations climate negotiations concluded in Antalya, Turkey, without a major new agreement after deep divisions arose over fossil fuels and climate finance. The talks became the longest in history but collapsed because the draft omitted direct references to phasing out fossil fuels and lacked concrete funding commitments for poorer nations. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres expressed deep disappointment over the deadlock.
articles.description: The prime minister of Australia, which co-hosted COP31, attributed the failure to "difficult geopolitical times".

articles.headline: Democrats secure historic House majority with at least 258 seats
articles.title: Democrats clinch a historic House majority of at least 258 seats, largest since 1992
articles.summary: House Democrats won at least 258 seats following a November 22, 2026 sweep, creating a divided government with a Republican White House and a Democratic Senate. Winning 44 additional seats, the party plans a 100-day agenda focusing on cost-of-living issues and oversight investigations. The outcome provides leadership under potential Speaker Hakeem Jeffries with a wide margin while reducing Republicans to 173 seats.
articles.description: Republicans will have at least 173 seats in the minority

articles.headline: Democrats win U.S. Congress control in midterm elections
articles.title: Democrats win U.S. Congress in midterm rout of U.S. President Donald Trump
articles.summary: Democratic candidates secured majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate during the midterm elections held on November 3, 2026. According to projections, the sweeping legislative gains hand the party power to block President Donald Trump's agenda, thwart judicial nominations, and investigate his administration. The wave of upsets included historic victories in reliably Republican strongholds such as Kansas, Iowa, and Texas.
articles.description: The Opposition party also retained key Senate seats, while victory in Georgia’s Governor race added to mounting signs that Republicans face a difficult night

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit collapses in Turkey after nations reject fossil fuel pact
articles.title: COP31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out

Australia led negotiations for a cover decision, but fierce opposition from countries including Ireland and the Marshall Islands resulted in a historic failure during the longest conference in UN history.
articles.description: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

articles.title: Iran strike wounds two in Bahrain, Riyadh denounces ‘criminal’ attacks
articles.summary: Bahrain accused Iran of targeting a civilian industrial facility on Sitra Island, causing a fire but no casualties, while two tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz. The incident occurred amid an ongoing maritime conflict and US counterblockade efforts. Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi stated a Qatari delegation visited Tehran for talks, as Tehran maintained its demands for lifting blockades.
articles.description: Bahrain said two people were wounded in an attack on “a civilian industrial site”, while Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they targeted U.S. air defence systems.

articles.headline: Climate talks end without deal after failing to secure consensus
articles.title: ‘Disappointing’: Delegates react after COP31 climate talks end without deal
articles.summary: United Nations climate talks concluded without an overarching agreement after negotiating blocs rejected a draft text presented by Turkiye and Australia. United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres expressed profound frustration over the outcome, citing opposition from oil- and gas-producing countries regarding fossil fuel references and adaptation finance targets.
articles.description: Draft text considered too weak to deal with climate change after oil-producing countries oppose the term 'fossil fuels'.

articles.headline: European Union rejects climate deal over lack of fossil fuel mention
articles.title: EU will ‘not endorse’ climate deal, throwing COP31 outcome into doubt

Ireland’s Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien stated the bloc would not endorse a pact that ignores the primary driver of climate change as negotiations extended into record extra time.
articles.description: Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien said the EU would not back an Antalya Pact that “does not even mention fossil fuels”, as the UN climate talks ran into record extra time

articles.headline: India and European Union expected to sign free trade agreement
articles.title: India-EU trade pact likely to be signed on December 16
articles.summary: India and the 27-nation European Union are likely to sign a major free trade agreement on December 16 during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Brussels. The deal, which follows two decades of negotiations, aims to provide duty-free access for 93 percent of Indian shipments and create a massive market for two billion people.
articles.description: European Union's Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, recently said the FTA will be signed during PM Modi's visit to Brussels in December, and it will come into force in 2027

articles.headline: Indian Parliament Winter Session history remains rare
articles.title: No Winter Session of Parliament? Skipped only four times in history
articles.summary: The Winter Session of the Indian Parliament has been skipped only four times throughout history, typically due to exceptional events like the Emergency or the COVID-19 pandemic. With the Monsoon Session remaining unprorogued for over 100 days, speculation has emerged regarding a potential special session to address the delimitation Bill, though no official confirmation has been provided.
articles.description: Each previous instance coincided with extraordinary disruptions, from the Emergency and Lok Sabha dissolutions to Indira Gandhi’s assassination and the COVID-19 pandemic

The Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs summoned Estonian charge d'affaires Marek Uhtegi on Monday to protest Tallinn's decision to close its border, while Estonian officials denied allowing their territory to be used for military operations.

articles.summary: India announced a $1.62 billion economic package to support Nepal following devastating August floods that killed over 1,300 people. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah confirmed the aid, which includes grants for infrastructure and credit for energy projects. The funding aims to assist reconstruction efforts after glacial collapses caused widespread destruction.
articles.description: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah is in New Delhi for a two-day visit — his first since coming to power in March.

articles.headline: Netherlands Foreign Minister calls for international rule of law
articles.title: Rule of law needed, not ‘Rule of Power’: Netherlands Foreign Minister Berendsen on trilateral summit
articles.summary: Netherlands Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen urged India and European nations to strengthen partnerships based on the international rule of law. Speaking during a visit to India, Berendsen suggested that these countries should act as a counterweight to the rule of power demonstrated by major nations during the recent trilateral summit held in Shenzhen, China.
articles.description: Berendsen holds talks with EAM Jaishankar, says Europe and India must end dependencies on global powers for energy, security and technology

articles.headline: Tajikistan notifies United Nations of its decision to withdraw from International Criminal Court
articles.title: Tajikistan moves to leave ICC amid US push against court
articles.summary: Tajikistan formally notified the United Nations of its decision to withdraw from the International Criminal Court, becoming the fourth nation to initiate departure since the United States urged countries to leave in July. The withdrawal from the Rome Statute will take effect on November 20, 2027. The International Criminal Court expressed concern following the announcement by the Central Asian nation.
articles.description: The ICC found that Tajikistan failed to comply with its request to arrest Russian President Vladimir Putin.

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit collapses over fossil fuel language
articles.title: What failure of COP31 reveals about a divided world
articles.summary: The COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, ended without an agreement after nations failed to reach a consensus on fossil fuel commitments. While roughly 130 countries demanded explicit language on transitioning away from fossil fuels, opposition from oil-producing nations and disagreements over climate finance prevented a final deal. The summit highlighted deep geopolitical divisions regarding climate action.
articles.description: Interests of oil-producing countries, a US boycott and a dispute over finance may have torpedoed climate talks.

articles.headline: Houthi officials report 17 deaths in Saudi-led coalition attack on Hodeida
articles.title: 17 killed in Saudi attack on Yemeni city: Houthis
articles.summary: Yemen’s Houthi movement reported that a Saudi-led coalition airstrike killed 17 workers and destroyed telecommunications facilities in Hodeida on November 23, 2026. The group’s Telecommunications Ministry stated the attack disrupted internet services for thousands. Separately, Houthis claimed a coalition strike in Lahj caused further casualties. Saudi Arabia has not commented on the reported incidents.

articles.headline: Oxfam report warns Israeli military attacks have contaminated Gaza environment
articles.title: Israeli attacks have turned Gaza into 'toxic wasteland', Oxfam says
articles.summary: A comprehensive report by Oxfam International and the Conflict and Environment Observatory reveals that Israeli military operations have severely contaminated the Palestinian territory with heavy metals, asbestos and untreated sewage. Amitabh Behar, executive director of Oxfam International, condemned the destruction as environmental war crimes. The Israeli government has previously rejected genocide accusations at the International Court of Justice, maintaining that its campaign is a self-defence measure against Hamas.
articles.description: The report says there are signs of possible contamination across almost all of Gaza as a result of Israel's actions.

articles.headline: Zelenskyy claims Ukrainian drone attack sank Russian warship in Libya
articles.title: Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship in Libya

Libyan officials confirmed the vessel was struck by drones on November 22, 2026, causing significant damage. Russia’s Defense Ministry has not provided a formal response regarding the status of the ship.
articles.description: The operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometres (1,500 miles) from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces

articles.headline: Israeli air strikes kill United Nations relief worker and two others in Gaza
articles.title: Israeli strikes kill at least three, including UNRWA worker, in Gaza

articles.description: Israel continues to launch attacks across the enclave, despite an October 2025 'ceasefire' deal.

articles.headline: Moscow warns Ukraine of consequences after drone attacks on Russian vessels

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that his forces sank two ships, including the corvette Merkury in Benghazi. articles.description: The Kremlin warns of an "escalation of tensions in the region", but declines to comment directly on the attacks in Libya.

Zelenskyy also reiterated his demand for Ukraine to join NATO, though Secretary General Mark Rutte noted that alliance members currently lack the unanimous support required.

articles.headline: Vina Nadjibulla says Modi visit will reset Canada relations
articles.title: Modi’s Canada visit is set to move ties in a new direction: Vina Nadjibulla
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's upcoming visit to Canada provides a vital opportunity to reset bilateral relations. articles.description: What has changed is that both governments appear increasingly willing to approach security issues through the lens of mutual security interests, rather than allowing these differences to define the entire relationship, says CEO of the Vancouver-based think tank

articles.headline: India pledges $1.6bn to Nepal to strengthen bilateral ties
articles.title: India pledges $1.6bn to Nepal in reset of ties
articles.summary: India has announced a $1.6bn support package for Nepal to bolster diplomatic relations and assist with post-flood reconstruction. The funding includes energy project credit and infrastructure grants. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepali counterpart, Balen Shah, also inaugurated a cross-border train service and secured new port access to improve connectivity between the two nations.
articles.description: As Nepal rebuilds after deadly floods, its prime minister sets contentious issues aside to secure Indian funding, port access and a new train service.

articles.headline: Iran vows to counter US naval blockade with all available means
articles.title: Iran says it will use ‘all available means’ to counter US blockade
articles.summary: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei stated on Monday that Tehran will use all necessary measures to challenge the US naval blockade. The blockade, restored in July following a collapsed agreement, has severely impacted Iran's oil exports. Iran maintains that the US actions constitute military aggression and claims it is entitled to self-defense under international law.
articles.description: Ministry of Foreign Affairs says Iran will use all tools to confront the naval siege and defend itself.

articles.headline: Democrats secure largest House majority since 1992 following North Carolina victory
articles.title: Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 after flipping North Carolina seat
articles.summary: The Democratic Party achieved its biggest House majority since 1992 after Chuck Hubbard defeated incumbent Republican Representative Virginia Foxx by 330 votes in North Carolina. The race was officially called on November 23, 2026, following a recount requested by Foxx. Hubbard campaigned heavily on local economic issues and the rising cost of living associated with the ongoing conflict involving Iran.
articles.description: Democrats have now won at least 258 seats in the midterms compared to Republicans, who hold at least 173 seats.

articles.headline: Supreme Court criticizes Bihar judge for convicting police superintendent

articles.headline: Global powers compete for mineral wealth across the African continent
articles.title: How the US, China and Russia are competing for Africa’s mineral wealth
articles.summary: The United States, China, and Russia are competing fiercely for Africa's critical mineral wealth, including cobalt in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and lithium in Mali. articles.headline: Ukraine reports drone strikes on Russian vessels near Libya
articles.title: Ukraine shares video of strikes on Russian ships off Libya
articles.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky released footage on Sunday appearing to show Ukrainian drone strikes against Russian ships off the Libyan coast. The attack reportedly sank a warship and damaged a cargo vessel allegedly transporting weapons. While the Kremlin warned of regional escalation, it did not directly address the incident, and local health officials confirmed receiving injured personnel.
articles.description: President Zelensky said a Russia warship was sunk, with a Russian cargo ship also hit.

articles.headline: UN climate talks collapse in Turkiye over fossil fuel disagreements
articles.title: COP31: What next after UN climate talks collapse
articles.summary: The COP31 climate summit in Antalya concluded in failure after participating nations deadlocked over phasing out fossil fuels and financing energy transitions for developing countries. Delegates and experts warned that the stalemate highlights persistent divisions and raises questions regarding the consensus-based negotiation process under the United Nations.
articles.description: UN member states fail to agree on how to fast-track action to reverse global warming in a blow to climate agenda.

articles.headline: Ukraine claims responsibility for naval drone attacks on Russian vessels
articles.title: Ukraine claims drone strikes on Russian ships off Libya: What do we know?
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed that naval drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury and struck the cargo vessel MV Angara off the coast of Libya. articles.headline: US congressional panel urges dialogue with India on Dalai Lama succession
articles.title: U.S. panel urges India dialogue for Dalai Lama succession, warns of China legitimacy contest
articles.summary: A bipartisan United States congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level diplomatic and intelligence channel with India to plan for the 14th Dalai Lama's succession. The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission warned that China might turn the reincarnation process into an international legitimacy contest, while urging the recognition of the Gaden Phodrang Trust as the sole authority.
articles.description: A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, arguing that China may turn the process into an international legitimacy contest

articles.headline: India and China hold second round of military talks in Arunachal Pradesh
articles.title: Why the second round of Corps Commander-level dialogue in Arunachal Pradesh matters

articles.description: The second round is aimed at establishing clearer engagement protocols between the two armies, preventing face-offs between patrol parties from escalating into larger confrontations and ensuring that communication channels remain open

articles.headline: Bangladesh government vows to arrest former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina
articles.title: Bangladesh vows to arrest ex-PM Hasina if she returns from India
articles.summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam stated that Bangladesh will arrest former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina upon her planned return in December 2026. Dhaka is currently seeking her extradition from India under an existing treaty. Ms Hasina faces a death sentence following a 2024 uprising, prompting renewed street protests and clashes across multiple districts by supporters of her banned Awami League political party.
articles.description: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam said Dhaka expects India to honour the extradition treaty, as Sheikh Hasina’s planned December return fuels political tension and street violence

articles.headline: Grameen Bank branches targeted in Bangladesh amid political unrest
articles.title: Why is Bangladesh’s Grameen Bank under attack?
articles.summary: Grameen Bank recorded 97 attacks on its branches and offices between November 10 and 23, according to internal memorandums. Managing director Sarder Akhter Hamed confirmed that attackers looted documents and destroyed records. Government officials and researchers attribute the violence to supporters of the ousted Awami League directing anger at founder Muhammad Yunus following the removal of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina from power in August 2024.
articles.description: Leading financial institution has found itself at centre of tensions amid violence by Sheikh Hasina supporters.

articles.headline: Palestinian landowners face severe access restrictions in West Bank military zones.
articles.title: Occupied West Bank ‘military zones’ become de facto Israeli settler land
articles.summary: Palestinian residents in the occupied West Bank face severe restrictions in accessing their ancestral lands after military zones and farm outposts effectively block their entry. Property owners report widespread destruction, theft and violence by Israeli settlers. Legal experts and human rights organisations note that such closures increasingly hand over territory to settlers despite official legal protections for local farmers.
articles.description: Closed military zones in the occupied West Bank are being seized by settlers as staging posts for pogroms.

articles.headline: India announces development package worth over ₹15,000 crore for Nepal
articles.title: India announces development package over ₹15,000 crore for Nepal’s development
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a development package of ₹15,000 crore on November 23, 2026, during talks with Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah in New Delhi. The leaders virtually launched multiple projects and a cross-border rail link. According to PM Modi, the funds aim to support Nepal's reconstruction and long-term prosperity following recent devastating floods, reinforcing bilateral ties.
articles.description: "The relations between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as the oceans," says Nepal’s PM

articles.headline: Russian strikes kill at least fifteen people across Ukraine's Kyiv region.
articles.title: At least 15 killed in Ukraine’s Kyiv region as Russia intensifies attacks
articles.summary: At least fifteen people died in Russian missile and drone strikes across Ukraine's Kyiv region, including eleven fatalities from a building collapse in Dymer. Emergency services worked to rescue survivors and search for missing residents while energy infrastructure was targeted. Meanwhile, Ukrainian drone attacks hit oil facilities inside Russia and Ukrainian forces sank a Russian corvette near Libya.
articles.description: Mulitple strikes unleashed days after Putin promises a ‘painful’ response to Ukrainian attacks.

articles.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine behind attacks on Russian ships near Libya
articles.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has claimed responsibility for an attack that sank the Russian ship ‘Merkury’.

articles.headline: Oxfam report blames Israel for toxic pollution across majority of Gaza.
articles.title: ‘Environmental crimes’: Israel blamed for toxic pollution in 99% of Gaza
articles.summary: A report by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory states that Israeli military operations have contaminated over ninety-nine percent of Gaza, creating a toxic wasteland with severe risks to human life. The bombardment generated millions of tonnes of rubble, destroyed water and sanitation plants, and released massive greenhouse gas emissions. The enclave's population faces poisoned water, unsafe soil, and acute shortages of basic supplies.
articles.description: A new report by UK-based charity Oxfam shows how Israel’s destruction of Gaza has created a ‘toxic wasteland'.

articles.headline: Prime Minister Andy Burnham defends landmark EU agreement in Parliament
articles.title: Burnham to tell MPs 'landmark' EU deal could make next decade 'much better'
articles.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham will tell Parliament on Monday that a new agreement with the European Union provides a realistic opportunity to improve the British economy over the next decade. The deal addresses food exports and emissions trading, though opposition leaders including Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch and Reform UK leader Nigel Farage sharply criticized the terms and economic projections.
articles.description: The prime minister will tell MPs the deal agreed on Friday is a "choice between a broken status quo or change".

articles.headline: Artificial intelligence market driven by massive infrastructure investments
articles.title: AI reality check: Leadership turmoil, IPO jitters and the fragility of big tech
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence has emerged as a major investment driver on Wall Street, with companies investing heavily in infrastructure to support the evolving technology. Nvidia corporation has become a central semiconductor supplier, while technology giants Microsoft, Amazon and Google have committed substantial funds toward data centre development, alongside artificial intelligence developers OpenAI and Anthropic.
articles.description: As financial markets begin to question the economics, reliability and sustainability of the AI revolution, the AI trade faces its most significant reality check yet

articles.headline: Supreme Court seeks responses on public interest litigation regarding anti-defection law reforms
articles.title: Supreme Court seeks response of Centre, ECI on PIL for reforms in anti-defection law
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on November 23, 2026, sought responses from the central government, the Election Commission of India and the Law Commission regarding a public interest litigation filed by A. Sethu. The petition raises concerns about the alleged misuse of strategic resignations by elected representatives to evade disqualification proceedings under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution.
articles.description: The PIL raised concerns over alleged misuse of resignations by elected representatives to circumvent disqualification proceedings and influence the survival of elected governments

articles.headline: Indian and Nepali prime ministers hold bilateral talks in New Delhi
articles.title: PM Modi holds bilateral talks with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah; trade, investment, connectivity on agenda
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah met at Hyderabad House on November 23, 2026, to review relations and expand cooperation in trade, energy, and infrastructure. Accompanied by a 34-member delegation, Mr. Shah also attended a business forum and paid tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at Raj Ghat during his two-day State visit to India, according to official reports.
articles.description: Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah, on a two-day State visit, laid a wreath at Raj Ghat and received a Guard of Honour at Rashtrapati Bhavan before the talks at Hyderabad House

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit ends without consensus after fossil fuel omissions.
articles.title: How did the COP31 climate agreement fall apart – and what happens now?
articles.summary: The COP31 global climate summit in Turkey concluded without a final agreement after the European Union rejected a draft text that omitted references to phasing out fossil fuels. Major oil producers Saudi Arabia and Russia blocked transition language, exposing deep divisions between developed and developing nations over finance and emissions cuts. Despite the stalled official negotiations, numerous countries and businesses backed alternative electrification and transition pledges outside the formal agenda.
articles.description: In a year of unprecedented climate disasters, a supercharged El Niño and as the world heads inevitably past 1.5 °C of warming, the EU and other nations said that the international process did not meet the moment

articles.headline: Alice Huang maintained contact with Chinese intelligence during Nvidia affair
articles.title: Alice Huang in touch with Chinese spy agency during affair with Nvidia CEO, says NYT
articles.summary: Alice Huang maintained communication with an intelligence officer from China's Ministry of State Security for over a year during her affair with former Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang. United States officials continue to investigate Huang and her former company Megaspeed International regarding advanced chip exports. The revelation follows Jensen Huang's resignation and has intensified scrutiny from lawmakers regarding export controls.
articles.description: Spokespersons for Nvidia, Jensen Huang and the Chinese Embassy ‌in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for ‌comment

articles.headline: Ukrainian forces launch drone attacks on Russian vessels near Libyan coast
articles.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine was behind drone attacks on Russian ships off Libya
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed that Ukrainian forces sank a Russian warship named Merkury and struck a cargo ship named MV Angara using naval drones off the coast of Libya on November 23, 2026. The United Nations Support Mission in Libya expressed serious concern over the incident and called for an immediate independent investigation into the attacks.
articles.description: President Zelenskyy says Ukrainian forces sank the Russian warship Merkury in an "exemplary" sea drone operation.

articles.headline: Marc Marquez secures record-equalling eighth premier-class world championship title
articles.title: MotoGP maestro Marquez makes history with eighth premier-class world title
articles.summary: Ducati rider Marc Marquez secured his eighth premier-class world championship at the Portuguese Grand Prix on November 23, 2026, after finishing eighth in the race won by Marco Bezzecchi. The 33-year-old Spaniard equalled Italian great Giacomo Agostini's historic record following a challenging season that required a remarkable comeback from injuries and surgeries.
articles.description: His eighth success in the premier class of motorcycling pulled Marc Marquez level with Italian great Giacomo Agostini.

articles.headline: Deadly attack in Kyiv as Russia launches barrage against Ukraine
articles.title: Deadly attack in Kyiv as Russia launches barrage against Ukraine

articles.headline: Divya Deshmukh wins women's Chess World Cup in Batumi
articles.title: Teenager Divya outlasts Humpy, emerges India’s first women’s World Cup winner
articles.summary: Nineteen-year-old Divya Deshmukh won the women's Chess World Cup in Batumi, Georgia, by defeating fellow Indian player Koneru Humpy in a tiebreaker on November 23, 2026. Alongside the title organised by the International Chess Federation, the victory earned the teenager her Grandmaster title, making her the fourth Indian woman to achieve the distinction.

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit ends without central political agreement on emissions
articles.title: Five takeaways from the failed climate talks COP31
articles.summary: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey concluded as the longest-running United Nations climate negotiations in history without delivering its central political agreement known as the Antalya Pacts. Co-hosted by Australia and Turkey, the talks collapsed amid deep geopolitical divisions, disputes over fossil fuel language, and disagreements regarding climate finance for developing nations.
articles.description: The COP31 summit in Antalya was the longest-running climate talks in UN history.

articles.headline: Russian strikes kill at least 15 people in Kyiv
articles.title: Ukraine says Russian strikes kill 15 in Kyiv region
articles.summary: Russian aerial barrages across the Kyiv region killed at least 15 people on November 23, 2026, as rescue workers searched through the rubble of a partially collapsed residential building in Dymer. Regional officials reported that strikes also hit a supermarket in Vyshneve and a private home in Bila Tserkva, while Moscow continued targeting energy infrastructure ahead of winter.
articles.description: Moscow has been pummelling Ukraine with nightly aerial barrages as the war-torn country braces for another winter, as the full-scale invasion grinds through its fifth year

articles.headline: Indonesian factory fire kills 24 people in Banten
articles.title: Indonesia says 24 killed in factory blaze as rescuers search for dozens missing
articles.summary: Indonesian authorities confirmed that 24 people died in a fire that broke out on November 21, 2026, at a confectionery factory in Cikande, Banten province. Rescuers continued searching through unstable structures for approximately 30 missing workers on November 23. Officials stated that preliminary investigations indicate the blaze may have been caused by an air-conditioner short circuit.
articles.description: Authorities ⁠were still investigating the cause of the fire, which broke out on Saturday (November 21, 2026) evening, in one building of the ‌PT Fonusa Agung Mulia confectionery factory in Cikande in Banten province, about an hour’s drive ‌from the capital Jakarta

articles.headline: Carlos Alcaraz defeats Alexander Zverev to win ATP Finals
articles.title: Alcaraz storms past world number one Zverev to win maiden ATP Finals title
articles.summary: Spanish tennis player Carlos Alcaraz defeated world number one Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 in the final to capture his first ATP Finals title. The 23-year-old saved three set points in the tiebreak on Sunday to secure his 14th consecutive victory and complete a dominant end to the season following previous tournament wins in Vienna and Paris.
articles.description: Alcaraz joins an exclusive list, becoming one of only four men to have won all four majors and the ATP Finals.

articles.headline: Trump says he wants ‘permanent’ deal to stop Iran getting nuclear weapons
articles.title: Trump says he wants ‘permanent’ deal to stop Iran getting nuclear weapons
articles.description: US President Donald Trump says he wants a permanent agreement to prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons.

articles.headline: Jasprit Bumrah leads India to historic Test victory against South Africa
articles.title: IND vs SA second Test | Fiery Bumrah helps Team India break a Cape Town hoodoo
articles.summary: India secured a seven-wicket victory against South Africa in Cape Town on January 4, 2024, to square the two-match series 1-1. Fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah took six wickets for 61 runs, dismantling the South African batting lineup in 642 balls. Aiden Markram scored a notable 106 runs for the hosts, while Shreyas Iyer hit the winning runs for the visitors.
articles.description: The pacer’s six-for sets up the visitors’ seven-wicket victory which also turns out to be the shortest in Test history; Rohit’s men win in 642 balls, bettering Australia’s 1932 record of 656 balls in Melbourne against the Proteas; teams share the series 1-1

articles.headline: Tata Steel approves twenty eight thousand crore asset sale to Apollo Tubes
articles.title: Tata Steel approves sale of tubes & pipes business, Tata Steel Colors to Apollo Tubes for ₹28,000 crore
articles.summary: The board of directors of Tata Steel approved agreements on November 22, 2026, to sell its steel tubes and pipes business along with its entire stake in Tata Steel Colors Pvt Ltd to APL Apollo Tubes Ltd for a combined transaction value of approximately twenty-eight thousand crore rupees. articles.headline: Mumbai Indians defeat Delhi Capitals to win inaugural Women's Premier League
articles.title: WPL final | Mumbai Indians defeat Delhi Capitals by 7 wickets to win the inaugural edition of Women’s Premier League
articles.summary: The Mumbai Indians secured the first-ever Women's Premier League title on March 26, 2023, by defeating the Delhi Capitals by seven wickets at Brabourne Stadium. Chasing a target of 131, Nat Sciver-Brunt scored an unbeaten 60 runs alongside captain Harmanpreet Kaur. Hayley Matthews and Issy Wong each took three wickets for the winning side during the match.
articles.description: Nat Sciver-Brunt smashed an unbeaten 55-ball 60, while skipper Harmanpreet Kaur made a 39-ball 37 as MI reached 134 for 3 in 19.3 overs

articles.headline: Physicians for Human Rights Israel reports surge in attacks on medics
articles.title: Israeli attacks on medics in occupied West Bank surge by 350%: Rights group
articles.summary: Physicians for Human Rights Israel documented a 350 percent surge in assaults against Palestinian healthcare workers in the occupied West Bank between 2022 and 2024. Report author Imran Anati stated that emergency medical staff regularly face intimidation, threats at gunpoint, and physical violence from Israeli soldiers and settlers, creating severe obstacles for emergency responses and urgent patient care.
articles.description: Physicians for Human Rights Israel says medics face 'dangerous escalation' in violence from soldiers and settlers.

articles.headline: Suspected Ukrainian sea drones strike Russian warship in Libyan naval base
articles.title: Suspected Ukrainian sea drones hit Russian warship at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say
articles.summary: Military officials reported that suspected Ukrainian sea drones struck the Russian Navy corvette Merkury at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya on November 22, 2026, causing a fire and explosion. Libyan authorities stated the vessel was docked for resupply under a bilateral agreement, while a joint investigation with Russia was launched to determine the source of the attack.
articles.description: The strike at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette, and ignited a fire at the facility, two Libyan military officials said

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit concludes without consensus on new deal
articles.title: What's next after no deal at COP31 climate talks?
articles.summary: The COP31 summit in Turkey officially ended without a consensus after participants rejected a fourth draft agreement. The European Union and other nations opposed the text because it failed to mandate a phase-out of fossil fuels, the primary driver of climate change. Negotiations broke down two days past their scheduled completion, marking the longest-running talks in the summit's history.
articles.description: The talks have been the longest-running in the summit's history, with negotiations breaking down two days after they had been due to end.

articles.headline: Seven-year-old boy rescued from rubble after Russian strikes in Ukraine
articles.title: Boy, 7, pulled alive from rubble hours after Russian strike on Ukraine, rescuers say
articles.summary: Emergency crews pulled a seven-year-old boy and a 79-year-old woman from the wreckage of a residential building in Dymer after overnight Russian strikes killed ten people in the Kyiv region on Sunday. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported that separate attacks across ten regions caused additional casualties, including three deaths in Vyshneve, as rescue operations continued amid ongoing air raid threats.
articles.description: Eleven people are dead in the attack on Dymer, with rescue efforts ongoing to find those still missing from the residential building.

articles.headline: BepiColombo spacecraft enters Mercury orbit amid reported thruster glitch
articles.title: Japan-Europe spacecraft BepiColombo begins orbit of Mercury, with a glitch reported
articles.summary: The European Space Agency and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency mission successfully placed the BepiColombo spacecraft into orbit around Mercury after an eight-year journey. European Space Agency officials confirmed that a software issue caused a shorter-than-planned thruster burn during the orbital maneuver. The spacecraft remains safe as mission teams at the European Space Operations Centre investigate the anomaly ahead of planned separations.
articles.description: The mission will seek to answer questions about Mercury such as why it has a magnetic field, why ice exists in the polar craters of a sun-scorched planet, and what is the nature of enigmatic depressions called "hollows" on its surface

articles.headline: Russian missile strike kills two people and injures 60 in Kryvyi Rih
articles.title: Russian strike kills two, wounds 60, in Zelenskyy’s hometown
articles.summary: An assault on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown in central Ukraine resulted in multiple casualties after missiles struck residential buildings and medical facilities. Local officials reported that emergency workers were subsequently hit by secondary blasts during rescue operations. The military escalation comes amid ongoing international diplomatic efforts involving United States President Donald Trump and Ukrainian leaders to negotiate an end to the ongoing armed conflict.
articles.description: Attack on Kryvyi Rih comes as Russian missiles land in NATO member Poland and US-led peace efforts face uncertainty.

articles.title: Child rescued in Ukraine after Russian drone attack kills 10
articles.description: A seven-year-old boy called David was rescued after spending 14 hours trapped in the rubble of a Russian drone attack.

articles.headline: India administers over one crore HPV vaccine doses to girls
articles.title: HPV vaccination campaign: Every dose is step towards protecting girls from cervical cancer, says PM Modi
articles.summary: India reached a healthcare milestone by administering more than one crore single-dose HPV vaccines to 14-year-old girls under a national campaign in under nine months. Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated on November 23, 2026, that every dose protects girls from cervical cancer. According to the Health Ministry, the voluntary initiative has achieved nearly 87% of its annual target at designated government facilities.
articles.description: India has administered more than one crore doses of the HPV vaccine to 14-year-old girls under its national vaccination campaign in less than nine months as on November 21

articles.headline: Nepal prime minister arrives in New Delhi for first official visit
articles.title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah arrives in Delhi for first official visit to India
articles.summary: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah arrived in New Delhi for his first official visit to India. articles.description: The PMs of India and Nepal are set to hold talks on Monday, with sources saying the discussion will give 'political direction' to bilateral relations for the coming years

articles.headline: India and China conclude talks to ease border tensions in Arunachal Pradesh
articles.title: India, China hold 10-day talks to ease LAC tensions in Arunachal Pradesh
articles.summary: India and China concluded a second round of military talks aimed at easing tensions along the Line of Actual Control in Arunachal Pradesh. The discussions, led by Lieutenant-General Girish Kalia and his Chinese counterpart, focused on establishing engagement protocols and preventing friction between deployed troops before the onset of harsh winter conditions.
articles.description: The talks focused on establishing engagement protocols, preventing face-offs and misunderstandings between troops deployed along the frontier, and maintaining open communication channels

articles.headline: Anthropic shares decline on Nasdaq following record initial public offering
articles.title: Anthropic’s stock market debut: a record IPO, a quick fade, decabillionaires, and the risks ahead | Explained
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence firm Anthropic launched its initial public offering on the Nasdaq on November 19, 2026, pricing shares at $83 before opening significantly higher at $111.50 and closing its debut at $97.17. The stock dropped 8.5 percent on its second trading day to close at $88.91 as trading volumes halved, highlighting investor questions regarding profitability and computing costs.
articles.description: The Claude maker’s shares surged on debut, valuing its founders’ stakes at billions, but soaring computing costs and the path to profitability remain key risks

articles.headline: Indonesian police recover 24 body bags after candy factory fire
articles.title: Indonesia confirms 24 killed in candy factory fire as search continues
articles.summary: Indonesian authorities are set to continue searching for 29 missing workers after police recovered 24 body bags from a gutted candy factory in Cikande, Serang regency. The fire broke out on Saturday evening at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia facility, where roughly 300 individuals were present. Officials noted that visual identification is impossible due to the fire's intensity, requiring DNA collection from relatives.
articles.description: Rescuers search for 30 people still missing.

articles.headline: US intelligence chief defends President Trump calling Vladimir Putin a friend
articles.title: US intelligence chief defends Trump’s comments calling Putin his ‘friend’
articles.summary: United States Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton defended President Donald Trump's description of Russian President Vladimir Putin as a friend during television appearances. Clayton asserted the language was appropriate for building personal rapport following a historic trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China. Meanwhile, critics and lawmakers raised concerns regarding United States foreign policy positions concerning Russia and Ukraine.
articles.description: US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton says Trump's comments were 'entirely appropriate' in context of summit.

articles.headline: Poland confirms second Russian assassination attempt targeting Ukrainian rapper
articles.title: Poland says Russia tried to assassinate Ukrainian rapper twice
articles.summary: Polish and Danish authorities stated that Russian intelligence services targeted Ukrainian-American rapper Albert Vasiliev, known as Kyivstoner, in two separate assassination plots. Polish officials confirmed an August 2026 plot in Poland and the arrest of a suspect, while Denmark reported a September attempt near Copenhagen, leading to the expulsion of a Russian diplomat. Russia dismissed the allegations as unsubstantiated.
articles.description: Polish confirmation comes after Copenhagen reveals alleged Russian plot to kill US-Ukrainian citizen on Danish soil.

articles.title: Israeli forces continue house demolitions in southern Lebanon

articles.headline: WHO chief urges peace in DRC following heavy fighting near Ebola hospital
articles.title: WHO chief calls for peace amid heavy fighting in Ebola-hit DR Congo region
articles.summary: World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus appealed for an end to hostilities after clashes in Ituri province disrupted medical operations. Health personnel and relatives were forced to shelter in a maternity ward for over a day. As of November 17, the Democratic Republic of the Congo recorded 5,678 fatalities from 11,613 cases, representing the nation's largest outbreak while ongoing violence complicates relief delivery.
articles.description: Fighting near a DRC hospital disrupts Ebola efforts, putting patients and workers at 'grave risk', WHO warns.

articles.headline: South Korean stock market tumbles amid mounting fears over artificial intelligence bubble
articles.title: Asian stock markets tumble as AI bubble fears mount
articles.summary: Asian financial markets experienced sharp declines as investors worried about the long-term viability of the artificial intelligence boom. Japanese markets remained closed for Labour Thanksgiving Day during the trading session.
articles.description: Stocks fall in South Korea and Hong Kong, as Wall Street set to rebound on Monday.

articles.headline: Trump criticises Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer amid upcoming leadership vote
articles.title: Trump criticises Schumer amid push for new Democrat leadership in US Senate
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump expressed opposition to Senator Chuck Schumer retaining his position as Senate majority leader in the incoming Congress. The debate highlights internal divisions within the Democratic Party following the November midterm elections. A closed-door ballot is scheduled for December 1, while Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen is mounting a challenge against the incumbent New York lawmaker.
articles.description: Schumer, who has led the Democrats since 2017, faces a challenge from Chris Van Hollen in his bid for majority leader.

articles.headline: Polish territory struck by suspected Russian missiles and drone
articles.title: Russian missiles hit Poland: What happened, and could NATO respond?
articles.summary: Polish officials stated that two missiles and a jet-powered drone landed in southeastern Poland during a heavy Russian bombardment of Ukraine. The incident prompted security concerns among North Atlantic Treaty Organization allies and coincided with ongoing diplomatic efforts involving the United States to negotiate an end to the conflict.
articles.description: Warsaw accuses Moscow of intentional provocation, but bar for triggering NATO's collective defence clause remains high.

articles.headline: Rescue workers recover bodies after Russian strikes in Kyiv region
articles.title: 'Danger seems greater all the time': Ukrainians search for missing after Russian strikes
articles.summary: Ukraine's State Emergency Services reported that at least three bodies were recovered from a residential building hit by a Russian strike in the Kyiv region. Rescue operations to locate trapped individuals faced continuous delays due to ongoing drone threats near the site. Emergency personnel successfully evacuated several residents earlier in the day amidst worsening security conditions.
articles.description: The BBC's Sarah Rainsford reports from the scene of a collapsed residential building in Ukraine's Kyiv region.

articles.headline: Democrats secure largest House majority since 1992 following North Carolina win
articles.title: Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 with North Carolina seat
articles.summary: The Democratic Party captured its largest House majority since 1992 after winning a closely contested North Carolina congressional seat in the November midterm elections. According to Associated Press reports, Democrat Chuck Hubbard narrowly defeated incumbent Republican Virginia Foxx. The historic gains in both the House and Senate provide Democrats significant leverage over President Donald Trump during the final two years of his term.
articles.description: At least 258 US House seats are now under Democratic control, with four more midterm races yet to be decided.

articles.headline: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot condemns settler attacks in West Bank
articles.title: Israel’s Eisenkot condemns arson attacks by Jewish settlers in West Bank
articles.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot denounced arson attacks and racist graffiti in Palestinian villages as Jewish terrorism, blaming the policies of ultra-nationalist cabinet ministers. articles.headline: Iran Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps downs two United States drones over Hormuz
articles.title: Iran says it downed US drones over Hormuz as bid to end war remains stalled
articles.summary: Iranian forces intercepted and shot down two United States drones over the Strait of Hormuz, according to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The incident occurred on Saturday amid ongoing military tensions and stalled diplomatic efforts to end the conflict. Gukesh acknowledged his rival's strong form and consistency, noting that the upcoming encounter will present a genuine test for his title defence.
articles.description: The first game of the best-of-14 match against Sindarov will be played on Tuesday

articles.headline: Virginia reports first measles-related death of 2026 in child

articles.summary: Virginia health authorities announced the state's first measles-related death of 2026 involving a child under five years old. The announcement arrived shortly after the United States lost its measles-free status, with national cases exceeding 5,800 this year. State officials confirmed 220 cases overall, predominantly among unvaccinated individuals, while federal agencies distribute additional funding to bolster vaccination and outbreak response efforts.
articles.description: The death comes within days of health experts stripping the US of its measles elimination status, amid uptick in cases.

articles.headline: Russian strike on Ukrainian apartment building kills two and wounds four

articles.summary: Authorities reported that a Russian military strike destroyed a five-storey residential building in Dymer, located north of the Ukrainian capital, on November 22, 2026. articles.description: Rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child, from the destroyed five-storey building in Dymer, while 11 were believed to be trapped under the rubble

articles.headline: Netanyahu and Eisenkot parties resume coalition talks in Israel
articles.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties resume talks to form Israel government
articles.summary: Delegations from Yashar and Likud met in Herzliya on November 22, 2026, to discuss forming a coalition government after recent elections failed to yield an absolute majority. Gadi Eisenkot has until December 6, 2026, to establish a government, though negotiations face significant hurdles regarding policy positions, leadership structures, and potential inclusion of Arab parties or ultra-Orthodox factions.
articles.description: Likud laid down conditions for a unity government, including no Arab parties and rejection of a Palestinian state, while Gadi Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government

articles.headline: Russian cargo vessel hit by drone attack in the Gulf of Finland
articles.title: Russia-bound ship towed away after it was attacked in Gulf of Finland
