articles.title: Croatia outraged after psychiatric patient dies from alleged hospital abuse
articles.description: Eight psychiatric workers have been arrested in Croatia on murder charges after images emerged of a patient being abused

articles.headline: India maintains consistent position on Indus Waters Treaty amid Delhi forum visit
articles.title: India says no change in its position on Indus Water Treaty as Pakistan minister attends SCO forum in Delhi
articles.summary: India stated that its stance on the Indus Waters Treaty remains unchanged during a media briefing by Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal on November 20, 2026. This development coincided with Pakistan Minister Musadik Malik visiting New Delhi to attend the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Purana Quila.
articles.description: India suspended the treaty in 2025 as one of the punitive measures against Pakistan after the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack last year that claimed 26 lives

articles.headline: Myanmar criticizes ASEAN peace plan review as unfair and imbalanced
articles.title: Myanmar calls ASEAN review of peace plan 'unfair and imbalanced'; questions bloc's treatment
articles.summary: Myanmar criticized the Association of Southeast Asian Nations for adopting an unfair and imbalanced assessment of its implementation of a five-point peace plan during the summit in Manila on November 15, 2026. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that the regional bloc disregarded its views and maintained discriminatory summit restrictions. ASEAN leaders previously reiterated concerns over insufficient progress in resolving the conflict triggered by the military takeover in February 2021.
articles.description: Myanmar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the review and recommendations adopted at the ASEAN Summit in Manila did not reflect the positive measures undertaken by the country

articles.headline: Denmark expels Russian defence attaché following alleged assassination plot in Copenhagen
articles.title: Denmark expels Russian diplomat over alleged plot to kill Ukrainian rapper
articles.summary: Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen announced the expulsion of Russia's defence attaché after intelligence officials uncovered a suspected plot to kill a Ukrainian rapper at a concert near Copenhagen. Danish police arrested two suspects linked to the conspiracy, while European leaders condemned the operation as aggressive Russian hybrid warfare.
articles.description: Copenhagen accuses Moscow of planning assassination with banned local gang; Russia says no evidence for allegation.

articles.headline: Congress proposes four-point formula for delimitation with INDIA bloc support
articles.title: Congress proposes four-point formula for delimitation, says INDIA bloc on board
articles.summary: The Congress party proposed a four-point formula for upcoming parliamentary delimitation, suggesting the retention of 543 Lok Sabha seats, the preservation of current state-wise distribution, the reservation of one-third of seats for women, and a twenty-five-year freeze on these arrangements. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh stated that all parties in the Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA) supported the approach, accusing the government of failing to consult the opposition.
articles.description: Party proposes retaining 543 Lok Sabha seats, existing State-wise distribution and a 25-year freeze, with one-third reservation for women

articles.headline: Prime Minister Narendra Modi calls cultural connect global peace guarantee
articles.title: PM Modi says cultural connect can guarantee global peace
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that cultural connections are the biggest guarantee of global peace while speaking at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation civilisational dialogue forum in New Delhi on Friday. The event features Pakistan's participation for the first time since a May 2025 conflict, with Pakistan represented by Federal Minister Musadik Masood Malik. Modi proposed that Shanghai Cooperation Organisation member countries collaborate on digitising and translating ancient texts.
articles.description: Cultural and civilisational cooperation will strengthen relations among various countries, says Modi at SCO forum; Pakistan Minister to address meet on November 21

articles.headline: NCW seeks investigation into rape and murder in Nagercoil
articles.title: NCW seeks report on rape and murder of woman inside stationary train in Nagercoil
articles.summary: The National Commission for Women requested a time-bound Tamil Nadu police investigation into the alleged rape and murder of a woman inside a stationary train at Nagercoil Junction railway station. Chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar called for CCTV footage preservation and security reviews after a body was found four days post-incident. The commission demanded an action taken report within seven days.
articles.description: Taking suo motu cognisance of a media report published on November 21 alleging the victim’s body was discovered four days after the incident, the Commission called for expeditious identification of the deceased and tracing of her family

articles.headline: Supreme Court dismisses Tamil Nadu petition for Cauvery River water shortfall
articles.title: What recourse does the lower riparian State have in the Cauvery dispute? | Explained
articles.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed an application filed by Tamil Nadu on November 20, 2026, which sought a shortfall of approximately 11.7 thousand million cubic feet of Cauvery River water from Karnataka. The court stated that granting the request would require it to assume the role of authorities specifically constituted to oversee water-sharing arrangements, concluding that such a course of action was inappropriate.
articles.description: What were the highlights of the two States’ positions? How did the CWRC and the CMMA assess the issue of deficit in realisation? What was the stand of the Authority on the issue of backlog? What is the recourse available to the lower riparian State now?

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh outlines master plan for Amaravati Economic Region growth
articles.title: Govt. promoting Amaravati Economic Region as Andhra Pradesh’s major growth engine
articles.summary: The Government of Andhra Pradesh has outlined a comprehensive strategy to develop the Amaravati Economic Region as a major growth engine, according to a master plan prepared by the Capital Region Development Authority. Spanning nine districts with a significant share of the state economy, the region features a substantial investment pipeline including major infrastructure and industrial projects targeted for finalisation by July 2027.
articles.description: Comprising nine districts spread across 44,817 sq. km and a GSDP valued at ₹6.23 lakh crore, the CRDA and its partners, LASA (Lea Associates South Asia) and PwC India, are advancing the AER Plan with a target to give it the final shape by July 2027

articles.headline: U.S. deportees face abuse and extortion by guards in South Sudan
articles.title: U.S. deportees in South Sudan went hungry as guards pocketed money from relatives, families say
articles.summary: Migrants deported by the United States to South Sudan have endured severe deprivation and extortion by guards who pocketed thousands of dollars sent by detainees families, according to relatives and lawyers. While the South Sudan Foreign Ministry denied the allegations, deportees described living in squalor and facing violence, highlighting the consequences of U.S. immigration policies involving countries struggling with poverty and corruption.
articles.description: Guards have solicited and received thousands of dollars from detainees' families, who were told the money would be used to improve conditions for their loved ones

articles.headline: Rishabh Pant scores century as India extends lead against New Zealand
articles.title: IND vs NZ 1st Test Day 4 Stumps: New Zealand trail by 233 after India’s mammoth 720/9 declaration
articles.summary: Rishabh Pant scored 128 runs during the morning session on Day 4 of the first Test at Basin Reserve on Sunday, November 22, 2026. India reached 629 for six at lunch, holding a lead of 261 runs against New Zealand. Pant's performance included surpassing Brendon McCullum's tally of Test sixes before he was dismissed by Rachin Ravindra.
articles.description: India’s 720 for nine was the highest total in a Test innings in New Zealand, eclipsing the home side’s 715 for six declared against Bangladesh at Hamilton in 2019.

articles.headline: Rebels kill fifteen civilians in northwestern South Sudan attack
articles.title: Rebels kill 15 in South Sudan
articles.summary: An attack by rebels in northwestern South Sudan on November 22, 2026, killed at least fifteen civilians and several cattle keepers, local sources told Agence France-Presse. A caretaker commissioner blamed fighters belonging to an armed group loyal to former first Vice-President Riek Machar. The country continues to grapple with violent conflicts rooted in political infighting and ethnic tensions since its independence in 2011.
articles.description: An official hinted at fighters loyal to the country's former first Vice-President Riek Machar, a longtime rival of President Salva Kiir who has been under house arrest since March 2025

articles.headline: Kerala planning board targets seven percent real economic growth
articles.title: Plan approach paper eyes leveraging heft of Keralam’s economy for 15th Five-Year Plan period
articles.summary: The United Democratic Front government in Kerala is targeting a seven percent real economic growth rate during the fifteenth Five-Year Plan period from 2027 to 2032. According to the State Planning Board approach paper, achieving this requires massive annual investments exceeding the state budget capacity. Planners intend to direct external capital toward productive uses to expand the state economy despite existing fiscal strains.
articles.description: The UDF government and the Planning Board have visualised a ‘partnership economy’ for building the economy up from ₹16 lakh crore to ₹28 lakh crore by 2031-32

articles.headline: United Nations conference fails to adopt legally binding rules for killer robots
articles.title: Why have UN efforts to regulate ‘killer robots’ stalled?
articles.summary: Member states meeting in Geneva under the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons failed to secure a mandate for a binding ban on autonomous weapon systems. Major military powers including the United States and Russia resisted the restrictions, agreeing instead to elaborate on a potential accord by 2028. Rights groups criticised the delay as putting civilians at risk.
articles.description: CWC countries agree to 'elaborate' on potential accord regulating autonomous weapons in two years, prompting criticism.

articles.headline: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah begins bilateral visit to India
articles.title: A new Nepal, an old neighbour - Balendra Shah's India test on first visit
articles.summary: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah arrived in Delhi for a two-day visit to meet Indian counterpart Narendra Modi, marking the first engagement between the new political generation and India. Discussions cover economic cooperation, energy, air corridors, and reconstruction aid following devastating flash floods in August that killed over 1,450 people. The visit aims to reset bilateral ties and address long-standing strategic, border, and trade differences.
articles.description: Trade, connectivity and regional cooperation will be on top of the agenda when Nepal's PM meets his India counterpart.

articles.headline: Gem and jewellery council urges balance between economic patriotism and cultural traditions
articles.title: Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural heritage: GJC on PM Modi’s call to stop gold purchases
articles.summary: The All India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council welcomed Prime Minister Narendra Modi's call to reduce gold imports and prioritise local products. Chairman Rajesh Rokde stated that while supporting restraint on bullion investment, the ten lakh crore industry must balance economic patriotism with cultural traditions during the upcoming festive and wedding seasons.
articles.description: The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) argued that the gold jewellery sector contributes nearly 7-8% to the economy and supports millions of livelihoods

articles.headline: Infant deaths rise in Attappadi as medical authorities examine ten cases
articles.title: In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare
articles.summary: Ten infant deaths have been reported this year in the tribal settlement of Attappadi, located in the Palakkad district of Keralam. Six of the cases involved congenital anomalies, including heart defects. An expert committee of researchers and doctors is currently examining the fatalities. Among the victims was five-month-old Dakshina, whose parents alleged that a cooperative hospital in Perinthalmanna withheld her body over unpaid medical bills.
articles.description: Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare. Poverty, land alienation, and the erosion of traditional food systems, are taking a toll on maternal and child health in this predominantly tribal region of Keralam

articles.headline: Narendra Modi expresses satisfaction over reduced gold purchases by citizens
articles.title: ‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed happiness on Saturday over reduced gold purchases following his previous year appeal, claiming this behavior caused prices to drop. Speaking at the fifth National Skill Convocation Ceremony in Indira Gandhi Pratishthan, he also predicted that skilled individuals will gain more value in the future job market than traditional certificate holders.
articles.description: PM Modi, referring to the fall in prices of gold, said, ‘A year ago, I had urged my fellow citizens that if they don't need it, please don't buy gold for a year’

articles.headline: Revanth Reddy compares electoral revision exercise to Simon Commission
articles.title: Simon Commission and SIR exercise are similar: Revanth Reddy
articles.summary: Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy likened the central government's electoral roll revision to the historical Simon Commission during a party meeting on Sunday. He alleged that seventy-one lakh votes were excluded, disproportionately affecting vulnerable communities. Furthermore, he urged the Centre to include caste enumeration in the upcoming national Census.
articles.description: Pointing out that Telangana had conducted an OBC caste census for the first time in nearly 100 years, he said the PAC should adopt a resolution urging the Union government to undertake a similar exercise nationally

articles.headline: Anthropic employee claims chatbot used to prove Riemann hypothesis
articles.title: In a year of AI solving maths problems, an Anthropic worker says he may have cracked the biggest
articles.summary: An Anthropic employee and mathematician stated that he used the non-public version of the company's Claude chatbot to create a detailed proof of the 170-year-old Riemann hypothesis over six weeks. Released in the Lean computer language, the proof spans more than 250,000 lines. Prominent mathematician Terence Tao noted that formal verification will take time, while other scholars have raised concerns regarding AI-driven mathematical claims.
articles.description: A mathematician at Anthropic says he used an AI to prove the famed Riemann hypothesis, though verification will take some time.

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit enters overtime amid fossil fuel deadlock
articles.title: Fossil fuel talks deadlock pushes COP31 climate summit into overtime
articles.summary: The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkiye, extended into overtime after nearly two million delegates remained deadlocked over a draft text that omitted fossil fuel phase-outs. The initial draft called for a faster transition away from fossil fuels, but references were removed following objections from Saudi Arabia and other major oil producers, drawing strong criticism from the European Union, Panama, and environmental groups.
articles.description: EU warns COP31 risks turning into a 'fossil summit' as critical climate commitments are omitted from the draft deal.

articles.headline: Fire continues on Russian cargo ship off Finland following drone attack
articles.title: Russian cargo ship still on fire off Finland after drone attack
articles.summary: A fire aboard the Russian cargo ship Sparta II continued burning in Finnish waters after a drone strike likely carried out by Ukraine. The sixteen crew members were evacuated, and vessels sprayed the vessel with water cannons overnight. Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo stated that the incident demonstrates how the war is spilling into the vicinity.
articles.description: The ship, bound for Russia's Kaliningrad, was damaged in international waters before drifting into Finnish territory.

articles.headline: Anupama Ramachandran defends world women snooker championship title in Indore
articles.title: Anupama successfully defends IBSF World Women’s Snooker Championship
articles.summary: India's Anupama Ramachandran successfully defended her International Billiards and Snooker Federation World Women's Snooker Championship title by defeating Hong Kong China's So Man Yan three to one in Indore on Saturday. She achieved history by becoming the first Indian woman to successfully defend the championship after overcoming tough competitors throughout the tournament.
articles.description: Reacting to the win, Anupama told The Hindu, I didn’t start very well in the final and I was a little nervous, but I did better

articles.headline: Telangana farmers face losses as banks miss agricultural credit targets
articles.title: Farmers suffer during kharif as banks did not achieve targets of agri credit
articles.summary: Agricultural producers in Telangana encountered severe difficulties during the kharif season due to an El Nino-induced monsoon deficit and a failure by banking institutions to meet loan disbursal targets. According to official data, banks achieved only 44.25 percent of short-term production loan goals during the first half of the financial year ending on September 30, raising concerns over future lending amid ongoing water shortages.
articles.description: With the government asking farmers to refrain from water-intensive crops in rabi, doubts are being expressed over the lending by banks in view of adverse weather conditions

articles.headline: India maintains winning chance in first Test against New Zealand
articles.title: IND vs NZ 1st Test Day 4: Jurel sees chance for India despite slowing Basin Reserve pitch
articles.summary: Wicketkeeper-batter Dhruv Jurel expressed optimism that India can force a result against New Zealand at Basin Reserve, despite a slow and low pitch. Speaking after Sunday's play on November 22, 2026, Jurel highlighted Rishabh Pant's 128-run innings and a mammoth total of 720/9 declared. He noted that bowlers need eight good deliveries in windy Wellington conditions to dismiss the hosts.
articles.description: The wicket is getting slow, day by day. It is also staying a little low, so we just need to be lucky. We need to bowl eight good balls, Jurel said after the penultimate day’s play

articles.headline: Global metal prices plunge to multi-month lows amid monetary policy concerns
articles.title: Gold, copper, aluminium dive to at least 7-month lows
articles.summary: Benchmark prices for gold, copper, and aluminium dropped to multi-month lows on November 21, 2026, driven by expectations of U.S. Federal Reserve interest rate hikes and shifting global macroeconomic conditions. Gold fell to 3,521.38 dollars per troy ounce at the London Bullion Market Association. Analysts attribute the correction to stronger U.S. dollar performance, rising treasury yields, and eased supply concerns.
articles.description: Hawkish commentary from U.S. Fed and concerns over global economic growth have been among the more prominent concerns.

articles.headline: Hebron project restores ancient wells to combat severe water shortages
articles.title: Restored wells bring life back to Hebron’s occupied Old City
articles.summary: Palestinian residents and institutions in the Old City of Hebron are combating severe water shortages by reviving traditional underground wells through a municipal restoration initiative. Implemented by the Hebron Rehabilitation Committee, the project has restored over one hundred wells to help families and schools maintain essential daily supplies and preserve their heritage amid ongoing movement restrictions.
articles.description: Hebron's Old City has been under constant siege by Israeli settlers and the military.

articles.headline: BJP president Nitin Nabin announces new national organisational team
articles.title: Nitin Nabin announces his team; Smriti Irani, Ram Madhav make a comeback, Amit Malviya out
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party President Nitin Nabin unveiled his national organisational team on August 17, 2026, seven months after taking charge. The new lineup features former Union Minister Smriti Irani returning as general secretary and former general secretary Ram Madhav returning as vice president. The appointments reflect continuity, organisational experience, and the impact of recent events on social media communications.
articles.description: The appointment with the most sharp signalling, however, appears to be in the BJP’s social media team. After a long stint at the helm, Amit Malviya will no longer be in charge. Deepak Mhaskey from Chhattisgarh replaces him.

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi quizzes newly appointed BJP office-bearers
articles.title: The new BJP team’s piecemeal reset
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi questioned sixty-four newly appointed Bharatiya Janata Party national office-bearers individually about their past organisational work during an August 22 meeting. Journalist Shekhar Iyer noted the new team reflects a shift toward prioritising capabilities over individual personalities. The restructuring highlights the party's political anxieties as it targets a fourth term in the 2029 general election.
articles.description: Apart from the usual distribution of organisational berths to poll-going States, caste groups, and other demographics of sex and age, the new BJP team reflects the party’s attempts at a reset. Nistula Hebbar reports on how three terms in power have brought both the pieties of the past and anxieties of the future into focus

articles.headline: University of Hyderabad students continue protests against faculty member over casteist remarks
articles.title: University of Hyderabad students continue protest, demand termination of faculty member over alleged casteist remarks
articles.summary: Students at the University of Hyderabad persisted with demonstrations demanding the termination of history department faculty member Vijaya Ramadas Mandala. Protesters accused him of publishing derogatory and casteist remarks in an email communication between April 14 and 16, 2026. The Students Union sought solidarity from parliamentarians and historians, while administration remained silent over the ongoing campus unrest.
articles.description: The email communication between April 14 and 16, 2026, contains references to former students from the Scheduled Castes community as “untouchables”, remarks against students from marginalised backgrounds in Bihar and Jharkhand, and Islamophobic comments

articles.headline: Adani Group secures power supply contract in West Bengal amid transparency concerns
articles.title: Adani Group forays into West Bengal’s power sector, Trinamool calls for transparency
articles.summary: Adani Energy Solutions Limited received a letter of award from West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Company Limited to supply 1,750 megawatts of renewable power for 25 years. The All India Trinamool Congress criticized the deal on social media, demanding transparency instead of preferential access. Power supply is scheduled to commence on July 1, 2028, following a competitive bidding process.
articles.description: Adani Energy Solutions Ltd. has received a Letter of Award from West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Co. Ltd. for supply of 1,750 MW of Renewable Energy Round-the-Clock power for a period of 25 years

articles.headline: Gukesh Dommaraju and Javokhir Sindarov begin World Chess Championship match
articles.title: Gukesh vs Sindarov: The youngest World Chess Championship in history
articles.summary: India titleholder Gukesh Dommaraju will defend his crown against Uzbekistan challenger Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva, Switzerland, from November 22 to December 12, 2026. Both competitors will be twenty years old, establishing this fixture as the youngest world championship match in history. The winner of the fourteen-game classical series will claim a share of a two point five million dollar prize fund.
articles.description: India's Gukesh defends his title against Uzbekistan’s Sindarov in up to 14 games in Geneva from November 22.

articles.headline: Max Verstappen wins F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix for third time
articles.title: Max Verstappen wins F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix for third time in four years
articles.summary: Red Bull racing driver Max Verstappen secured victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix for the third time in four years following a chaotic race on Saturday. McLaren competitors Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri placed second and third respectively, while Mercedes driver George Russell crashed late in the event. The dramatic race featured numerous lead changes and challenging slipstreaming conditions for the competing drivers.
articles.description: Red Bull's Verstappen dug deep to fend off Antonelli and Russell in a race that saw a jaw-dropping 35 lead changes.

articles.headline: BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Wadkute dies of cardiac arrest in New Delhi
articles.title: BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Wadkute dies of cardiac arrest in Delhi
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party Rajya Sabha member Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute died following a cardiac arrest at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences in New Delhi at age 72. Admitted on November 20 after experiencing a cough, he suffered a heart attack and passed away on November 21, 2026. President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed condolences for the leader from Maharashtra.
articles.description: Hailing from Parbhani in Maharashtra's Marathwada region, Mr. Wadkute was elected to the Rajya Sabha in April this year

articles.headline: Indonesian sweets factory fire kills three people and leaves 36 missing
articles.title: Indonesia factory fire kills three, 36 missing
articles.summary: A devastating fire at the Fonusa Agung Mulia sweets factory in Banten province has left at least three individuals dead and 36 others unaccounted for. According to the National Search and Rescue Agency, rescue personnel successfully evacuated 15 people following the disaster. Firefighting teams continue operations at the facility, which produces Milkita snacks and is located near Jakarta.
articles.description: At least 15 people rescued, including 4 taken to hospital, as authorities say cause of the fire is under investigation.

articles.headline: Hemant Soren urges Chief Justice of India to appoint Jharkhand High Court successor
articles.title: Hemant Soren writes to CJI to urgently appoint Jharkhand HC Chief Justice successor
articles.summary: Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren wrote to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and the Supreme Court Collegium requesting an urgent successor for Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice M.S. Sonak, who retires on November 27. Soren warned that frequent transitions and interim arrangements disrupt administrative continuity, affecting institutional planning and judicial establishment certainty.
articles.description: Jharkhand CM asserted that the High Court of Jharkhand has repeatedly experienced short leadership tenures and interim Acting Chief Justice arrangements at the helm.

articles.headline: Power station fire in southern Iraq kills at least four
articles.title: Iraq fire at Basra power station kills at least four, injures 30
articles.summary: At least four people were killed and thirty injured in a fire at the Hartha power station north of Basra on November 21, 2026, according to security officials. Civil defence teams brought the blaze under control after it spread to neighbouring houses and halted operations at the facility, which had been operating at 400 megawatts.
articles.description: Civil defence ‌teams brought the fire at the Hartha ‌power station north of Basra ‌under ⁠control after firefighters responded ⁠to the incident, says Iraq’s state news agency

articles.headline: Nine pilgrims killed in vehicle collision with truck in Rajasthan
articles.title: Road crash in Rajasthan leaves nine dead
articles.summary: At least nine individuals lost their lives and several others sustained injuries when a vehicle carrying sixteen pilgrims crashed into a parked truck on the Kota-Udaipur highway in Rajasthan. Local administration officials stated that the victims were members of the same family returning to Maharashtra from a pilgrimage when the fatal road accident occurred.
articles.description: According to Additional District Collector Rajesh Joshi, the vehicle was carrying 16 people who were returning to Maharashtra after visiting Khatu Shyam when the accident occurred in the middle of the night

articles.headline: South Korea education minister resigns following artificial intelligence cheating scandal
articles.title: South Korea Education Minister resigns amid AI cheating scandal
articles.summary: Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned after an artificial intelligence-assisted cheating scandal preceded the national college entrance exam known as the Suneung. President Lee Jae Myung accepted the resignation of the seventy-two-year-old minister following public backlash over comments made regarding exam security, while authorities identified one hundred eleven misconduct cases involving electronic devices during testing.
articles.description: The country has been gripped by fears of AI-assisted exam cheating since last Sunday (November 15, 2026), when the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam confessed to using a miniature camera and smartphone to achieve a near-perfect score

articles.headline: Beijing criticises United States ban on telecom phone number access
articles.title: China slams ‘malicious’ U.S. ban on telecom firms’ phone number access
articles.summary: China denounced a decision by Washington to restrict Chinese telecom giants from accessing American phone numbers, labelling the move as malicious. The Federal Communications Commission approved the order to prevent illegal robocalling campaigns by bad actors. Affected companies include state-owned enterprises China Unicom, China Telecom and China Mobile, prompting Beijing to warn that it may implement necessary countermeasures.
articles.description: Affected entities include China’s three biggest telecom firms, the state-owned China Unicom, China Telecom and China Mobile

articles.headline: Kansas City Current defeat Washington Spirit to win NWSL title
articles.title: Kansas City Current defeat Washington Spirit 2-1 to lift first NWSL title
articles.summary: Kansas City Current secured their first championship title by defeating the Washington Spirit in the National Women's Soccer League final. Vanessa DiBernardo opened the scoring directly from a corner kick, and Debinha added a second goal during stoppage time at Audi Field. Despite a late header from Trinity Rodman, Kansas City maintained their lead to claim the victory.
articles.description: Trinity Rodman left in tears after scoring Spirit's only goal as DiBernardo and Debinha give Current a closely fought win.

articles.headline: India plans undersea cable network to connect eight Andaman islands
articles.title: PANI project to connect Andaman's eight islands through undersea cable network
articles.summary: The Centre is considering initiatives to strengthen digital connectivity across the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, including an undersea cable network connecting eight islands and an expansion of 4G mobile services to 87 uncovered villages. Proposals were discussed during a meeting between Union Telecommunications Secretary Amit Agrawal and Lieutenant-Governor Dinesh Sharma, according to a Lok Niwas release on November 21, 2026.
articles.description: The project is expected to address mobile and internet connectivity challenges in remote islands and ensure more reliable communication, particularly during emergencies

articles.headline: Police rescue two abducted girls in Bhadohi and arrest suspects
articles.title: Minor girls abducted, raped in Bhadohi, UP, rescued; one girl remains missing
articles.summary: Police rescued two minor girls and arrested two suspects following the alleged abduction and rape of three girls in the Bhadohi district. The victims, aged 14, 15, and 16, went missing after leaving for school on bicycles. A third 16-year-old girl and her alleged abductor remain missing as authorities continue search operations.
articles.description: Out of the three minors, two girls have been rescued but the third girl, 16, and the suspect who allegedly abducted her, remain missing, police said

articles.headline: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi attends multilateral summits in Manila
articles.title: Key takeaways from the Quad, ASEAN-India, and East Asia Summits in Manila | Explained
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi participated in three multilateral meetings on November 21, 2026, during the Association of South East Asian Nations summits in Manila. The events included the ASEAN-India Summit, the East Asia Summit, and the Quad Summit alongside leaders such as United States President Donald Trump, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese.
articles.description: Narendra Modi’s multilateral ASEAN engagements showed a growing desire to work more closely with the grouping at a time when global powers are working in a more unilateral manner

articles.headline: Proposed Kenyan internet metering bill sparks privacy and cost concerns
articles.title: Kenya’s internet metering bill raises privacy and affordability concerns
articles.summary: A proposed law requiring internet service providers in Kenya to monitor data consumption and introduce meter numbers has drawn opposition from industry and civil society groups over privacy and affordability concerns. Sponsored by MP Marianne Jebet Kitany, the Kenya Information and Communications Amendment Bill aims to make consumption-based billing mandatory for consumers.
articles.description: Kenya’s proposed internet metering law has prompted concerns over privacy, surveillance and rising connectivity costs.

articles.headline: Displaced Darfur families face severe winter hardships amid aid cuts
articles.title: Displaced Darfur families face volatile winter as Sudan aid cuts bite
articles.summary: Displaced families in Sudan are facing severe winter conditions without adequate shelter, blankets, or heating due to significant humanitarian aid funding shortages and ongoing conflict. According to United Nations agencies and the International Organization for Migration, millions require emergency assistance, but funding shortfalls have forced humanitarian organizations to severely scale back their support.
articles.description: Sudan's displacement crisis could worsen with winter approaching.

articles.headline: International Court of Justice rules Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority
articles.title: News in Frames | Living with the wounds of displacement
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority during military operations in Rakhine State. The historic decision follows a 2017 military crackdown that forced over seven hundred forty thousand Rohingya to flee to Bangladesh, where approximately one million two hundred thousand refugees currently reside in overcrowded camps.
articles.description: The ICJ ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya is significant, but refugees continue to face the threat of violence and restrictions on humanitarian access, as the situation in their homeland remains precarious

articles.headline: Three successive cyclones form over Bay of Bengal within twenty-three days
articles.title: Three cyclones in three weeks: What’s happening in the Bay of Bengal? | Explained
articles.summary: Three cyclones formed over the Bay of Bengal within a 23-day period, including Cyclone Arnab, Murasu, and Akvan, which made landfall in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha. According to meteorological reports, the unusual frequency is driven by weakening vertical wind shear and warm waters as the southwest monsoon withdraws, creating favourable atmospheric conditions during the primary October-December cyclone season.
articles.description: Such a frequency is uncommon but not unique this year; there were around 1.8 cyclones a year in the post-monsoon period in 1982-2022, with the average increasing after 2001

articles.headline: ICE agents detain two people at Seattle airport
articles.title: ICE agents detain two people at Seattle airport
articles.description: Masked ICE agents detained two people on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle as passengers were boarding a flight.

articles.headline: Assam activist Pranab Doley detained under national security law
articles.title: Pranab Doley | Confronting the State
articles.summary: Assam grassroots organiser Pranab Doley spent 118 days in detention under the National Security Act following his opposition to a luxury hotel project near Kaziranga National Park. The 40-year-old leader of the Jeepal Krishak Shramik Sangha has a history of arrests stemming from his ongoing legal battles for indigenous land rights in the region.
articles.description: The rights activist in Assam is asking why indigenous people are being criminalised while defending their land and heritage

articles.headline: Factory fire in Indonesia leaves three dead and thirty-six missing
articles.title: Fire at Indonesian candy factory leaves 3 dead, dozens unaccounted for
articles.summary: A devastating fire at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia candy factory in Serang district, Banten province, resulted in three fatalities and left thirty-six workers unaccounted for. Rizky Dwianto of the Banten Search and Rescue Agency reported that emergency personnel rescued fifteen individuals while continuing firefighting and cooling operations more than twelve hours after the blaze began.
articles.description: The blaze broke out at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia factory in Serang district, in Banten province, which borders Jakarta

articles.headline: First images of Mexican cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’ after arrest
articles.title: First images of Mexican cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’ after arrest
articles.description: First images of Mexican cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’ after arrest

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh achieves national recognition for HIV control
articles.title: Andhra Pradesh gets national recognition for its progress in HIV/AIDS control
articles.summary: Sixteen districts in Andhra Pradesh have attained national recognition for progress in HIV control, with six districts reaching Surakshit status and ten achieving Saksham status. The rankings reflect performance on targets established by the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS to end the epidemic by 2030. State Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav attributed the success to enhanced monitoring via the Suraksha portal and targeted community initiatives.
articles.description: Six districts in the State have achieved ‘Surakshit’ status and another 10 the ‘Saksham’ status, and the rankings are based on a district’s performance on 95-95-95 targets fixed by the Joint United Nations Programme

articles.headline: Emmanuel Bacry warns hospitals lack capacity to assess healthcare AI
articles.title: Healthcare AI: hospitals lack capacity to measure real-world patient outcomes, warns French expert
articles.summary: Emmanuel Bacry, Scientific Director of France's Health Data Hub, stated at the Bengaluru Tech Summit that global hospitals cannot adequately measure real-world patient outcomes from artificial intelligence. Speaking on November 20, 2026, he warned that most training data is Western-centric and highlighted the risks of deploying unadapted tools without proper clinical integration protocols.
articles.description: Emmanuel Bacry warns that laboratory accuracy scores do not establish real-world clinical benefits; says healthcare AI trained largely on Western data may not work elsewhere

articles.headline: Eleven killed during Mexican military operation to capture cartel leader
articles.title: Eleven killed in burst of violence during Mexican cartel leader’s capture
articles.summary: An overnight military operation in Guasave resulted in eleven deaths, including seven alleged cartel gunmen and four soldiers, during the capture of cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores. The Mexico Defence Ministry confirmed that Meza Flores, alongside two other suspected members, was apprehended and transferred to Mexico City following violent clashes involving roadblocks and burning vehicles.
articles.description: Seven alleged cartel gunmen and four soldiers were killed in operation to arrest cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores.

articles.headline: Delhi Police apprehend 14-year-old hacker for selling Agniveer data
articles.title: 14-year-old used AI chatbot to hack Agniveer ‘test’ website, wanted to earn money by selling it on dark web: Delhi police sources
articles.summary: The Delhi Police Special Cell apprehended a 14-year-old boy from Ballabhgarh for allegedly hacking a test website and attempting to sell personal data belonging to approximately 4,000 Agniveer personnel on the dark web for 500 US dollars. Investigators recovered data from his devices and contacted the Union Ministry of Home Affairs to verify its authenticity, while the juvenile was handed over to his family.
articles.description: The Haryana teenager used an AI chatbot to identify valuable data and find a way into the test portal; preliminary investigation suggests only names and addresses were accessed, Delhi Police sources say

articles.headline: Nigerian funeral boat capsizes resulting in twenty-four deaths
articles.title: Overturned boat carrying mourners to funeral kills at least 24 in Nigeria
articles.summary: Authorities in Nigeria confirmed that twenty-four people died after an overloaded wooden vessel transporting mourners to a burial service capsized due to a mechanical failure in Bayelsa State. Emergency responders stated that rescue operations remained active, with local divers assisting police who arrested the vessel manager after the driver fled. The tragedy highlights ongoing safety concerns regarding passenger transport on domestic waterways.
articles.description: Police say the boat driver fled and the vessel’s manager was taken into custody.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu solar energy generators anticipate installation slowdown next year
articles.title: T.N. may see solar energy installations slowing down, say energy generators
articles.summary: Industry representatives warned that Tamil Nadu could experience a deceleration in solar energy installations due to administrative delays and escalating expenses. Stakeholders cited an ineffective single window clearance system, pending regulatory clarity on the Battery Energy Storage System policy, and unexpected banking charges as primary factors hindering ongoing project development.
articles.description: In the last one month, some of the solar energy generators received notices demanding 8% banking charges.

articles.headline: Bessent confirms he’s living on US military base over Iran fears
articles.title: Bessent confirms he’s living on US military base over Iran fears
articles.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says he’s still living at a US military base, two weeks after an Israeli warning.

articles.headline: Mehbooba Mufti criticises authorities for dumping municipal waste in Pampore saffron fields
articles.title: Kashmir’s famed saffron fields have been used as dumping grounds for three years: Mehbooba Mufti
articles.summary: Former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Mehbooba Mufti stated that Kashmir's saffron fields in Pampore, Pulwama, have served as a municipal dumping ground for three years. She said nearly two thousand kanals were damaged and 150 families faced livelihood threats. The National Green Tribunal recently directed a joint committee inspection to assess pollution impacts and check for statutory clearances.
articles.description: The former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister says nearly 2,000 kanals of land have been damaged, threatening the livelihoods of 150 families; the NGT has directed a panel to inspect the site and recommend action

articles.headline: Moviegoers head for the exits as quake strikes Peru
articles.title: Moviegoers head for the exits as quake strikes Peru
articles.description: Moviegoers head for the exits as quake strikes Peru

articles.headline: Young Nigerians face financial and political barriers in upcoming elections
articles.title: Nigerian youth have shown their power in the past - why aren't they shaping this election?
articles.summary: Abdulhadi Dalhatu is among the young candidates running for office in Nigeria's upcoming general elections in January. Although about eighty percent of the population is under forty, high nomination fees and campaign costs hinder youth participation. Major political parties have set steep fees, while voter registration among citizens under thirty-five has declined.
articles.description: Fewer young people have registered to vote in next year's election than in 2023 - are young people losing faith in democracy?

articles.headline: Teen gamer and mother help rescue missing girl held in Oregon
articles.title: How a teen gamer and his mother helped rescue a missing girl
articles.summary: Sixteen-year-old Landon Tresp and his mother Khristina helped rescue a seventeen-year-old girl who had been missing for over a year. After chatting online, the victim revealed she was held against her will by Adam Hunter Harmel in Oregon. Khristina located the address using property records and coordinated with the Federal Bureau of Investigation to secure her release.
articles.description: When 16-year-old Landon Tresp met a teenage girl in an online game, it led to him and his mother helping the FBI rescue her from kidnapping.

articles.title: Iran faces a ‘silent economic war’, says Iranian president
articles.description: Iran faces a ‘silent economic war’, says Iranian president

articles.headline: India and Bulgaria review bilateral ties and regional security during talks
articles.title: India, Bulgaria discuss bilateral ties, IMEC, Black Sea situation
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Bulgarian counterpart Velislava Petrova met at Hyderabad House in Delhi on November 22, 2026, to assess cooperation across trade, security, and technology. The officials also discussed connectivity projects including the India Middle East Europe Economic Corridor, alongside the Ukraine conflict and the Black Sea situation, aiming to strengthen broader diplomatic and economic exchanges.
articles.description: ‘Our teams have drawn up a detailed roadmap of cooperation, so we will be approving that today, and I think that will give a very clear pathway to our activities ahead,’ said S. Jaishankar

articles.title: Impunity fuels surge in settler violence across occupied West Bank
